questions.q: Describe the main features of the imperial capital of Vijayanagara.
answer: Vijayanagara, meaning the city of victory, was the magnificent capital of the empire of the same name, founded in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra, at the site now called Hampi.

answer.text: The city was protected by massive stone walls and gateways enclosing not only the town but also its farmland. To supply so large a population, elaborate arrangements were made for water, including the great Kamalapuram tank and the Hiriya canal for irrigation.
The royal centre held the audience halls and the raised Mahanavami Dibba, from which the king watched the grand Mahanavami festival, along with the elegant Lotus Mahal and the elephant stables.
The sacred centre had splendid temples such as the Virupaksha and the Vitthala, the latter famous for its stone chariot and musical pillars, with towering gateways called gopurams.

answer: The ruins at Hampi still reflect the wealth and artistry of this great capital.
